sources.catena: St Thomas Aquinas, Catena Aurea on St Matthew and St John (Oxford trans., 1841)
sources.marmion: Bl Columba Marmion OSB, Christ in His Mysteries (1924)
sources.liguori: St Alphonsus Liguori, The Glories of Mary (1888)
sources.denis: Denis the Carthusian, Enarratio in Canticum Canticorum (1898), trans. from the Latin for Still

scripture.text: Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to the Jordan, unto John, to be baptized by him.

meditations.body:
Picture the riverbank before anything happens:
a line of people waiting their turn,
each one there because of something they have done.
Tax collectors, soldiers, the ashamed of three provinces —
a queue defined by its confessions.
And into that line, unannounced,
after eighteen years of sawdust and silence,
steps a carpenter from Nazareth.
He mingled with the multitude of sinners.
No herald, no distance, no exception made.
The public life of the Son of God begins
with Him taking a place in the sinners' line —
which is to say, in yours.
Stand in the queue with Him for this decade.

scripture.text: But John stayed him, saying: I ought to be baptized by thee, and comest thou to me?

meditations.body:
The Baptist's protest speaks for every one of us.
He is overruled.

scripture.text: And Jesus answering, said to him: Suffer it to be so now. For so it becometh us to fulfil all justice. Then he suffered him.

meditations.body:
What is this justice that must be fulfilled?
Name the double office Christ fills in every mystery.
He is Son of God, before whom the angels veil their faces —
and He is Head of a fallen race whose flesh He has taken.
As Son, He could claim the right hand of the Father this instant.
As Head, He will enter heaven only at the front of His people,
having passed through everything owed by them.
So the just one stands in for the unjust — justus pro injustis —
and His humiliation here renders to Infinite Holiness
the supreme homage that pays our whole debt.
The baptism of penance, received by the sinless,
is the down payment on Calvary.

scripture.text: But our God is in heaven: he hath done all things whatsoever he would.

meditations.body:
Here is the mystery's great reversal, and it has never wavered:
He did not go down into the water to be washed by it.
He went down to wash it.
The East sings it every Theophany —
today the nature of the waters is sanctified —
and the icon paints the psalm literally:
the Jordan turning back at His feet, the sea seeing and fleeing.
Say it plainly:
sanctified by contact with the Humanity of Jesus,
the water received the virtue of washing away sins.
Every font in every parish church draws its power from this moment.
He stepped into the river,
and every baptism that would ever be performed
became possible on the spot.

scripture.text: And the earth was void and empty, and darkness was upon the face of the deep; and the spirit of God moved over the waters.

meditations.body:
The Bible's first sentence about the Spirit
has Him moving over the face of the waters,
on the eve of the first creation.
Now, over the waters of the Jordan, He appears again —
and the rhyme has always been read:
this is day one of the new creation,
begun the way the first one was,
Spirit over water, about to speak light.
Even the dove carries a memory.
The last time Scripture showed one over the waters,
it was searching a drowned world for somewhere to rest,
and finding nowhere.
This dove descends and remains.
The long flight over the flood is finished.
There is finally a place on earth for the Spirit to land.

scripture.text: And Jesus being baptized, forthwith came out of the water: and lo, the heavens were opened to him: and he saw the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming upon him. And behold a voice from heaven saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

meditations.body:
Watch the divine law written across this scene in three strokes.
Christ stoops to mingle with sinners —
and forthwith the heavens open to magnify Him.
He asks for the baptism of penance —
and the Spirit descends to testify He possesses grace in plenitude.
He presents Himself as one deserving the strokes of justice —
and the Father declares He takes all His delight in Him.
Every humiliation answered instantly by a glorification:
humiliavit semetipsum, propter quod exaltavit.
You have met that arc at the crowning with thorns and at the Ascension.
This riverbank is where it is first performed in public,
as the signature of how God works.

scripture.text: And behold a voice from heaven saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

meditations.body:
Attend to the timing of the Voice.
This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased —
spoken before a single miracle, a single sermon, a single disciple.
Thirty years of hidden life,
of sawdust and obedience and nothing the world would call achievement,
and the Father's delight is already total.
The belovedness does not follow the performance; it precedes everything.
The same sentence will sound on Thabor at the summit of glory,
and it holds even at the Ecce Homo, over the disfigured face.
It was never earned and it never wavers.
Rest inside that sentence for the length of this decade.
It is the ground the whole Gospel stands on.

scripture.text: The next day, John saw Jesus coming to him; and he saith: Behold the Lamb of God. Behold him who taketh away the sin of the world.

meditations.body:
The first public title of His ministry
is the name of a sacrifice.

scripture.text: Then he went down, and washed in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God; and his flesh was restored, like the flesh of a little child: and he was made clean.

meditations.body:
The Jordan had a résumé before that morning.
Centuries earlier, Naaman the Syrian — a great man, and a leper —
was told by the prophet to go wash seven times in this same river.
He nearly refused; the rivers of Damascus were better water.
But he went down,
and came up with his flesh restored like the flesh of a little child.
Read it as the rehearsal it was:
a proud man, a humbling instruction, an unimpressive river,
and skin like a child's — which is to say, a man born again.
The Jordan had been practicing for the Baptism of Christ,
and every baptism since gives what Naaman got:
the flesh of a little child,
fit for a kingdom that only children enter.

scripture.text: For as many of you as have been baptized in Christ have put on Christ.

meditations.body:
This mystery is not a scene you watch but an inheritance you hold.
Your baptism was conferred in the Name of the Trinity —
the Trinity revealed to the world on this riverbank:
Father's voice, Son in the water, Spirit descending.
And what the sacrament did is the whole Gospel in one sentence:
from children of wrath it made us children of God,
so that we are henceforward, with Jesus, though in lesser measure,
the objects of the heavenly Father's delight.
As His baptism was the summary of His mission,
so yours contains in germ your whole Christian life.
As many as have been baptized in Christ have put on Christ —
and no one has ever taken Him off you.

scripture.text: Therefore will I distribute to him very many, and he shall divide the spoils of the strong, because he hath delivered his soul unto death, and was reputed with the wicked: and he hath borne the sins of many, and hath prayed for the transgressors.

meditations.body:
Isaias had prophesied that the Servant would be reputed with the wicked —
counted among the transgressors.
Most readers place that on Calvary, between the two thieves,
and it belongs there.
But look where the counting begins:
in the water queue at the Jordan,
where anyone taking a census of sinners that morning
would have written His name in the ledger with the rest.
The solidarity that ends between two crosses
starts in a river line, chosen freely, decades early.
He was never caught among sinners. He enrolled.
And He has never asked to be taken off the list,
because the list is where you are.

scripture.text: And I will pour upon you clean water, and you shall be cleansed from all your filthiness, and I will cleanse you from all your idols. And I will give you a new heart, and put a new spirit within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and will give you a heart of flesh.

meditations.body:
Everything this mystery holds happened to you personally,
on a specific day, at a specific font,
when clean water was poured upon you and a heart of flesh was given.
So here is the decade's question, and it is disarmingly practical:
do you know the date?
Most Catholics can name their birthday to the hour
and have never once asked when they were baptized.
Yet that was the day the Voice said beloved over you.
Find the date this week —
a parish record, a family Bible, a phone call to your mother.
Write it down.
Keep it the way you keep the birthday it outranks.

scripture.text: And immediately the Spirit drove him out into the desert. And he was in the desert forty days and forty nights, and was tempted by Satan. And he was with beasts: and the angels ministered to him.

meditations.body:
Mark gives the sequel one shocking adverb:
immediately — statim —
the Spirit drove him out into the desert, to be tempted.
Do not soften it:
the same Spirit who descended as a dove now drives;
the Father's beloved is sent straight from the affirmation into the combat.
And the lesson holds for every baptized soul:
temptation is not the evidence that grace has failed
but the field where constancy is proven —
eternal life is the recompense of those who,
having had to choose, resisted and remained faithful.
If your consolations keep being followed by battles,
the pattern is not broken.
It is the pattern.

scripture.text: Behold what manner of charity the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called and should be the sons of God. Therefore the world knoweth not us, because it knew not him.

meditations.body:
Behold what manner of charity:
that we should be called, and should be, the sons of God.
Not called only — should be.
The Voice at the Jordan spoke over you at your font,
and it has not retracted.
Yet most of us live the day in the opposite order:
perform first, and maybe feel approved by nightfall.
So take the mystery's harder question into the week ahead:
what would you attempt — what would you finally rest from —
if the approval were already settled?
Because it is.
Beloved is not the wage at the end of your day.
It is the ground you woke up standing on.

scripture.text: Now it came to pass, when all the people were baptized, that Jesus also being baptized and praying, heaven was opened.

meditations.body:
Luke alone preserves the detail
that makes this a closer for people who pray:
Jesus being baptized and praying, heaven was opened.
Not at the water's touch — at the prayer.
The sky opens over a man praying,
which is precisely what you are at this moment.
So end the decade there:
under an opened heaven, in the posture that opened it.
Tomorrow the public life begins —
the roads, the crowds, the desert first of all —
and it begins from prayer,
the way everything He did began from prayer.
Rise from this decade the way He came up from the river:
beloved, anointed, and headed somewhere.

scripture.text: And the third day, there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee: and the mother of Jesus was there. And Jesus also was invited, and his disciples, to the marriage.

meditations.body:
Notice how the Evangelist orders the guest list:
the mother of Jesus was there — and Jesus also was invited.
Draw the human inference:
they invited Him not as a great person but as one they knew,
one of the many; as they invited the mother, so they invited the Son.
In Cana He is still somebody's relative —
Mary's boy, welcome because she is.
And He came.
The public life that will end on a Roman cross
begins at a village wedding, among ordinary joy,
because He cared more for our good than for His own dignity.
Take your seat at the feast for this decade.
You were invited the same way — through His mother.

scripture.text: And the wine failing, the mother of Jesus saith to him: They have no wine.

meditations.body:
The shortest intercessory prayer in Scripture:
a fact, laid at His feet.

scripture.text: And Jesus also was invited, and his disciples, to the marriage.

meditations.body:
Do not let the scene pass without its scandal:
let the proud man blush to see the humility of God —
the Son of the Virgin comes to a marriage,
He who, when He was with the Father, instituted marriage.
And press the consequence:
if the marriage bed honestly kept partook at all of sin,
our Lord would never have come to one.
So the three states of life each receive their honor in His story —
born of a virgin, blessed in infancy by the widow Anna,
and now attending a wedding as a guest.
Whatever your state — married, widowed, single, consecrated —
He has stood inside its blessing personally.

scripture.text: He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: and he as a bridegroom coming out of his bridechamber, Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way:

meditations.body:
Now lift the whole feast into the heavens:
what marvel that He went to that house for a marriage,
who came into this world for a marriage?
For here He has His spouse, whom He redeemed with His own blood —
the Word is the Bridegroom and human flesh the bride,
and the womb of the Virgin Mary was His bridal chamber,
from which He came forth as a bridegroom, as the psalm had sung.
Rest inside that for the decade:
the Incarnation itself was a wedding, your nature the bride,
and Cana is the Bridegroom attending a small copy of His own mystery —
smiling, perhaps, at how much the guests don't know about weddings.

scripture.text: And the wine failing, the mother of Jesus saith to him: They have no wine.

meditations.body:
Fix on the detail that defines her forever:
nobody asked her to intervene.
She saw the trouble of that young couple —
the small, mortifying, utterly unspiritual disaster
of wine running out at your own wedding —
and moved only by her compassionate heart,
which cannot look upon the afflictions of others without pity,
she went to her Son unrequested.
Then hand the inference on:
if she is so ready to help when no one asks,
what will she do when someone does?
Who has ever invoked this sweet Lady, and not been heard?
Her résumé begins with an unsolicited kindness about wine.
It has never changed character since.

scripture.text: Lord, all my desire is before thee, and my groaning is not hidden from thee.

meditations.body:
Study the shape of her prayer,
because it is a whole school of petition in four words:
they have no wine.
No instructions.
No proposed solution, no timetable, no 'therefore you should.'
She states the need and stands back —
Lord, all my desire is before thee —
trusting the Person more than any plan she could attach.
Most of our prayers are the opposite:
fully engineered requests with the outcome pre-drawn,
disappointed in advance by any other answer.
Hers leaves the whole solution space to Him,
and receives more than anyone at that feast could have specified.
Tonight, take your heaviest intention and try her grammar:
the fact, laid at His feet, and nothing else.

scripture.text: And Jesus saith to her: Woman, what is that to me and to thee? My hour is not yet come.

meditations.body:
Woman, what is that to me and to thee?
The words sound cold until you walk around them.
Some argue from this verse that she was not His mother —
but the same Evangelist wrote the mother of Jesus was there;
both stand or neither.
Remember Nazareth:
He was subject to His parents; no one honored her more.
Then take the key:
the answer marks the line between His manhood, which she bore,
and His Godhead, which she did not —
you did not beget that in Me which works the miracle.
He speaks here as God about to act as God.
The mother is not being dismissed.
The Divinity is being disclosed.

scripture.text: But Jesus answered them, saying: The hour is come that the Son of man should be glorified.

meditations.body:
My hour is not yet come.
Hear in that sentence a promise with a date on it:
I will acknowledge thee, He says to her in effect,
when the infirmity of which thou art the mother shall hang upon the cross.
The hour is Calvary — and when it came, He did exactly that:
from the cross, the same address, Woman, behold thy son.
What was deferred at the feast was paid in full at the execution.
And a thunderclap follows,
against the astrologers who seized on the verse:
the hour was not of destiny but of will —
the Maker of the stars is not under the dominion of the stars.
Neither are you.
His hour, and yours, belong to Providence, not the horoscope.

scripture.text: His mother saith to the waiters: Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye.

meditations.body:
Now watch what she does with an answer that sounds like no.
She does not argue, repeat herself, or retreat hurt.
She turns to the servants with complete serenity:
whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye —
as if the yes were already in motion,
because she knows the Person well enough
to hear it inside the apparent refusal.
It is the boldest act of faith in the chapter, and it worked.
These are also the last words of hers that Scripture records —
her final sentence in the Gospels is an instruction to obey Him —
and they are the sentence this whole Rosary ends on.
She spent her one remaining line pointing at Him.
She has never needed another.

scripture.text: And the third day, there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee: and the mother of Jesus was there.

meditations.body:
Read the setting like a map of salvation.
The third day:
the world's first age was lit by the Patriarchs,
the second by the Prophets,
and the third — under grace — by the Gospel;
the marriage happens on the third day
because the Bridegroom has now appeared in the flesh.
Even the village name preaches:
Cana means desire of migrating,
and those most worthy of Christ are those who burn to pass over —
from vice to virtue, from earthly things to eternal.
And the wine was made to fail
to give our Lord the opportunity of making better.
Read your own failures by that light once, and see what they were for.

scripture.text: Jesus saith to them: Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.

meditations.body:
Look at what the miracle asked of the humans in the room:
fill the waterpots with water.
Six stone jars that stood there for the purifying of the Jews —
the old covenant's washing equipment —
and the task is plain manual labor,
twenty or thirty gallons apiece, hauled from the well.
They filled them up to the brim, John notes, and the brim matters:
they did the ordinary thing completely.
Water was their whole contribution; wine was entirely His.
That is the standing ratio of grace:
He asks for what you have, done to the brim —
the full jar, the honest day, the whole rosary —
and the transformation is none of your business.
Your business is the well and the brim.

scripture.text: And when the chief steward had tasted the water made wine and knew not whence it was, but the waiters knew who had drawn the water: the chief steward calleth the bridegroom,

meditations.body:
John plants one clause in parentheses
and it may be the most quietly thrilling in the chapter:
the chief steward knew not whence it was —
but the servants which had drawn the water knew.
The head table tasted excellence
and drew a wrong conclusion about the bridegroom's cellar.
The staff, wet to the elbows from obedience,
were the only people in Cana who knew what God had just done.
It is the standing economy of the kingdom:
the secret goes to whoever carried the water.
So the decade's question:
where in your life has humble obedience already let you in
on something the important people at the head table cannot see?

scripture.text: He brought me into the cellar of wine, he set in order charity in me.

meditations.body:
Why did she, alone in that room, expect wine from Him?
There is a reason deeper than confidence.
The Canticle's wine-cellar was read as her own soul,
the King saying:
not only did I bring thee into the cellar of wine, O most blessed Lady,
but into the Wine itself —
immersed wholly in the abyss of His riches and delights,
at the Annunciation, at the conception, at His birth.
The gloss is not about Cana; the application is ours —
but it fits like a key:
the woman who says they have no wine
is the one person present
who has been steeped in the Wine for thirty years.
She asks for wine from inside it.
So does everyone who prays from communion rather than toward it.

scripture.text: And saith to him: Every man at first setteth forth good wine, and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse. But thou hast kept the good wine until now.

meditations.body:
The steward states the world's economics
without knowing he is prophesying:
every man sets forth the good wine first,
and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse.
That is the shape of every merely earthly pleasure —
best at the start, diminishing forever after.
Then his astonishment: but thou hast kept the good wine until now.
That is the shape of grace, and it runs the other way:
the best is later, always later,
kept deliberately for the far end of fidelity.
So the question, especially if your life feels past its best vintage:
what would change this week if you actually believed
the Bridegroom's cellar works in that direction —
that for you, too, the good wine is kept until now?

scripture.text: This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee and manifested his glory. And his disciples believed in him.

meditations.body:
This beginning of miracles:
of all the signs He could have opened with —
a healing, an exorcism, something urgent —
the first is a hundred and more gallons of superb wine
for a party already well underway.
The glory of God is first manifested in joy multiplied past all need.
And the frame holds to the end of the Bible:
the ministry that opens at a wedding closes at a supper
where He takes wine and gives it a new name,
and history itself ends, John will write,
at the marriage supper of the Lamb.
Cana is the first course of that feast.
His disciples believed in him, the verse finishes —
over wine, at a wedding.
End the decade believing the same way: glad.

scripture.text: And after that John was delivered up, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God, And saying: The time is accomplished and the kingdom of God is at hand. Repent and believe the gospel:

meditations.body:
Mark gives the public preaching its first sentence, and every clause lands.
The time is accomplished — all the waiting of Israel,
prophets and psalms and four silent centuries, arrives at one Galilean afternoon.
The kingdom of God is at hand — not a program to be built but a proximity to be met,
near because the King is near, standing in sandals on the lake road.
Repent, and believe the gospel — turn, and treat this as news.
Notice what the ministry's first imperative is not:
it is not achieve, or organize, or even love. It is turn around.
Begin the decade by doing only that:
turn the face of your attention toward the One announcing,
and let the announcement be news to you again.

scripture.text: And he saith to them: Come ye after me, and I will make you to be fishers of men. And they immediately leaving their nets, followed him.

meditations.body:
He explains nothing; He invites everything.
And the nets drop immediately — the kingdom's first act of worship is an interrupted workday.

scripture.text: From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say: Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

meditations.body:
The Douay keeps the old rendering: do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
Notice what the first sermon is not.
He does not straightway preach righteousness, which all knew,
but repentance, which all needed — for repentance corrects the will,
and no one is left to plead: I desire to be good, but am not able.
And in this first address there is nothing severe, nothing burdensome —
no axe laid to the root, as John had preached —
but first things merciful, the glad tidings of the kingdom.
Smile at the geography too:
He does not say the kingdom of the Canaanite or the Jebusite is at hand.
The Law promised worldly goods. The Lord opens with heaven.

scripture.text: And Jesus walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea (for they were fishers).

meditations.body:
Do not let the guest list of the apostolate be prettified.
He chose not kings, senators, philosophers, or orators,
but common, poor, and untaught fishermen —
and so bowed the necks of the proud, gaining an Emperor by a fisherman:
great was Cyprian the pleader, but Peter the fisherman came before him.
Now weigh the price of admission.
Peter and Andrew had seen no miracle and heard no promise of reward,
yet at a single bidding left all — and he leaves much who keeps nothing for himself.
God does not weigh the sacrifice by how much is offered, but out of how much:
the kingdom is not valued at a certain price;
whatever a man has, much or little, is equally available.
Your much-or-little qualifies.

scripture.text: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, and that preacheth peace: of him that sheweth forth good, that preacheth salvation, that saith to Sion: Thy God shall reign!

meditations.body:
Gospel is a genre before it is a book:
evangelium, the herald's word,
the runner cresting the ridge with a report from the field —
not advice about how the war might yet be won, but news that it has been.
Isaias saw the messenger's feet on the mountains and called them beautiful
because of what the mouth above them carries:
peace, salvation, thy God shall reign.
Centuries later, Galilee heard the report delivered in person.
This is the difference the mystery turns on:
good advice asks something of you first;
good news announces something done for you first, and asks only to be believed.
Most of us quietly file the gospel under advice.
For one decade, file it where the herald filed it — under headlines.

scripture.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

meditations.body:
The kingdom's constitution opens with its door price, and the price is emptiness.
The first beatitude strikes at the root:
pride is the source of all evil, and humility the firm foundation —
if this be well laid, other virtues may be built on it;
if it be sapped, whatever good you gather perishes.
The Greek is blunter still: the poor here are literally they who beg —
blessed are those who stand at God's almshouse and know it.
And the ledger closes in one line:
the proud seek an earthly kingdom; of the humble only is the kingdom of Heaven.
Every other realm on earth is entered by what you have.
This one is entered by what you finally admit you lack.

scripture.text: And being asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God should come, he answered them and said: The kingdom of God cometh not with observation. Neither shall they say: Behold here, or behold there. For lo, the kingdom of God is within you.

meditations.body:
Asked when the kingdom would arrive, He answered where instead:
not with observation, not behold here or behold there —
the kingdom of God is within you.
The first meaning of the kingdom is a Person, and the Person has moved in.
That is the resting place of this decade.
You are not scanning the horizon for something delayed;
the King has made an address of you.
All the searching energy you spend on elsewhere and later —
He is asking for it back,
redirected a very short distance inward,
where grace has already taken up residence.
So stop traveling for the length of these ten beads.
The kingdom you are praying for is nearer than the beads in your hand.

scripture.text: And behold they brought to him one sick of the palsy lying in a bed. And Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the man sick of the palsy: Be of good heart, son, thy sins are forgiven thee.

meditations.body:
Watch whose faith moves the miracle.
Jesus, seeing their faith — not the sick man's, but theirs that bore him.
If borrowed faith availed to heal a man within and without,
of how great power with God must a man's own faith be?
Then the address. O wonderful humility:
this man feeble and despised, crippled in every limb, He calls son.
And pardon comes before cure for a reason:
by as much as the soul is better than the body,
by so much is forgiving greater than healing —
the visible lesser miracle is worked to prove the invisible greater one.
You have carried people to Him on these beads before.
The stretcher works.

scripture.text: Go then and learn what this meaneth, I will have mercy and not sacrifice. For I am not come to call the just, but sinners.

meditations.body:
Here the riverbank policy of the Baptism
becomes the kingdom's published mission statement.
Accused of dining with the wrong ledger entries,
He sends the accusers back to their own Scriptures:
I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.
Mind the grammar: God does not contemn sacrifice, but sacrifice without mercy.
Then the sentence that defines the ministry:
I am not come to call the just, but sinners.
Hear the consolation inside it, for everyone the call ever reached:
so far am I from abhorring sinners, that for their sakes only did I come.
Sinners are called as the sick are — by a physician, to be cured.
He enrolled in the sinners' queue at the Jordan.
Now He announces He came for the queue.

scripture.text: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a treasure hidden in a field. Which a man having found, hid it, and for joy thereof goeth, and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.

meditations.body:
The parable's economics are strange until you audit them.
The treasure is found without cost —
the preaching of the Gospel is open to all —
but to possess it with its field is not without price,
for heavenly riches are not obtained without the loss of this world.
Free to find; everything to keep.
And the currency of the purchase is not grim resolve:
if you do not sell your all you will not obtain it —
and this you ought to do with joy.
The man in the parable is not tightening his belt;
he is trying not to laugh at the terms.
Hide the find, too — guard it even from human praise, for robbers work the road.
Whoever sells everything grinning has understood this mystery.

scripture.text: Again the kingdom of heaven is like to a merchant seeking good pearls. Who when he had found one pearl of great price, went his way, and sold all that he had, and bought it.

meditations.body:
Why does the merchant's liquidation look effortless?
Because whoever has once known the sweetness of the heavenly life
readily leaves all he loved on earth —
everything that pleased him before appears to have lost its beauty,
for the splendour of that one pearl alone fills his mind.
Desire is not suppressed; it is outbid.
Then the parable turns inside out:
the pearl's preciousness is the possession of ourselves —
for while we were involved in the things we owned, we were not our own —
and so, having sold all, we give ourselves for the pearl,
not because we are of equal value, but because we cannot give anything more.
Read that twice.
The final price of the kingdom is you;
and the first thing the kingdom hands back is you.

scripture.text: And rising up, he came to his father. And when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion and running to him fell upon his neck and kissed him.

meditations.body:
His most famous portrait of repentance has almost no repenting in it.
The son's speech is barely begun; the plot belongs to the father —
who saw him while he was yet a great way off,
which means the old man had been watching the road,
and who runs, which patriarchs in that world did not do,
and falls on his neck before the rehearsed confession is out.
Luke gives the parable its setting:
it is Jesus' answer to the murmur
this man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them —
the father's portrait doubles as the Son's self-defense,
for our Elder Brother sought sinners out and sat at their feasts.
So the decade's question is the practical one:
when did you last let the Father run — when were you last in a confessional?
If the answer embarrasses you, name a day this week.
He watches the road.

scripture.text: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

meditations.body:
He did not leave the proclamation to heralds;
He planted it inside the prayer He taught,
second petition from the top: thy kingdom come.
The kingdom's arrival is the thing His people ask for
before they ask for bread —
before food, forgiveness, or rescue, the reign.
It also means you have been proclaiming this mystery all evening without noticing:
every decade of this Rosary opens with an Our Father,
so ten beads from now you will say thy kingdom come again.
Say it that time as what it is —
not filler before the Hail Marys but a citizen's daily oath,
the shortest act of allegiance in the language.
The kingdom comes, among other routes, through people who keep asking it to.

scripture.text: Another parable he spoke to them: The kingdom of heaven is like to leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until the whole was leavened.

meditations.body:
Of all the kingdom's portraits, the least dramatic:
leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal,
until the whole was leavened.
The method is hiddenness; the ambition is totality.
Nothing about the lump looks different at first —
but nothing in it is finally exempt.
Notice too that the leaven does not lecture the dough.
It is simply present, and presence does the work.
So the decade's question:
name your three measures of meal —
the household, the desk, the street you actually live on —
and then name honestly the one measure you have been keeping unleavened,
the corner where the kingdom is welcome to be believed but not to spread.
What would it mean, this week, to be kneaded in there rather than merely announced?

scripture.text: Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom.

meditations.body:
After the selling and the buying,
the treasure and the pearl and the price of everything,
the last word on the kingdom's transfer is none of these.
It hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom —
give, to a flock, and a little one.
All the leaving of nets turns out to be the unclenching of hands
so that something could be placed in them.
And fear not stands at the front of the sentence
because fear is what little flocks feel, and the Father legislates against it.
He kept a promise about this:
some standing here, He said, would see the Son of Man in His kingdom
before tasting death —
and six days later, three of the little flock were climbing a mountain.
That is the next decade.
End this one small, gifted, and unafraid.

scripture.text: And after six days Jesus taketh unto him Peter and James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into a high mountain apart:

meditations.body:
The words "after six days" count from a promise.
Only days earlier He had said:
some of you standing here will not taste death
until you see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.
Six days later, three of them are climbing.
Thabor is the promise kept early.
The short delay was long enough
to kindle the desire of the chosen three into full flame,
and short enough that the others felt no sting of jealousy.
There is something deeper in the number itself.
In six days the whole visible world was made.
Whoever would see the glory of the Word
must climb above the world it took six days to create.
Climb with the three for this decade.
The promise includes sight.

scripture.text: And he was transfigured before them. And his face did shine as the sun: and his garments became white as snow.

meditations.body:
The sun shines by no borrowed light.
Unveiled for an hour, neither does He.

scripture.text: And he was transfigured before them. And his face did shine as the sun: and his garments became white as snow.

meditations.body:
Where did the radiance come from?
Not from without. This was not a borrowed light
but an overflowing of the Divinity upon the holy Humanity —
an irradiation from the furnace of eternal life ordinarily hidden in Christ.
Then the sentence that reframes the whole hidden life:
for love of us, Jesus habitually hid the divine life
under the veil of mortal flesh,
preventing it from overflowing in a continuous light
that would have blinded our feeble eyes.
At the Transfiguration, the Word gave full liberty to His eternal glory.
Read that again slowly.
Thirty years of Nazareth ordinariness were not the absence of glory
but mercy about its wattage.
The veil was for you.
On Thabor, for one hour, He trusts three men with the furnace door open.

scripture.text: And behold there appeared to them Moses and Elias talking with him.

meditations.body:
Why these two visitors? Count the reasons.
The crowds had guessed Elias or one of the prophets —
so let the chief of the prophets stand there,
that the difference between servants and Lord be seen.
The standing charges were breaking the Law and usurping God's glory —
so He summons the Lawgiver himself
and the prophet most jealous for God's glory as character witnesses.
Moses is dead and Elias never died —
so His writ evidently runs on both sides of death.
And, tenderest of all: they spoke of His decease at Jerusalem —
glory convened to talk about the cross,
two men who had stood before Pharao and Achab
keeping Him company on the road toward a Roman governor.
Be meek as Moses. Be zealous as Elias.

scripture.text: And Peter answering, said to Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

meditations.body:
Read Peter's real estate proposal as a loving scheme.
Rebuked once for saying be it far from thee,
he dares not repeat it openly, so he suggests the same covertly:
three tents, permanent residence —
for if they stay on the mountain, He does not go up to Jerusalem,
and if He does not go up, He does not die.
It is the Passion, filibustered with camping equipment.
The theology needs one gentle correction:
do not set the servants level with their Lord —
and if you must build, build one tabernacle,
for Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, in thy bosom.
Yet defend the impulse underneath:
if Peter was so ravished by this glimpse,
what will it be to behold the King in His proper beauty?
The desire was right. Only the address was wrong.

scripture.text: And as he was yet speaking, behold a bright cloud overshadowed them. And lo a voice out of the cloud, saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear ye him.

meditations.body:
On Sinai the cloud was dark, for the Lord came threatening;
here it is bright, for He sought not to terrify but to teach.
Now watch the weld this Rosary has been waiting for.
At the baptism of Christ the whole Trinity appeared:
the Son in the flesh, the Spirit as a dove, the Father in the voice.
At the transfiguration, sacrament of the second regeneration,
the whole Trinity again:
the Father in the voice, the Son in the man, the Spirit in the bright cloud.
The dove marked baptism's gift, innocence;
the cloud marks resurrection's —
the refreshment and brightness of the rising bodies.
Jordan and Thabor are one mystery at two altitudes,
and your font, whatever its zip code, was the lower slope of this mountain.

scripture.text: And as he was yet speaking, behold a bright cloud overshadowed them. And lo a voice out of the cloud, saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear ye him.

meditations.body:
The Voice says what it said at the river — with one addition,
and the addition contains all the secret of our life:
Ipsum audite. Hear ye Him.
It is as if, to make us attain to Him, God simply referred us to Jesus.
So keep this testimony of the Father
ever present before the eyes of the heart —
reading the Gospel, visiting Him, receiving Him —
the words habitually before you: this is my beloved Son.
The sentence that opened over the Jordan's hiddenness
holds over Thabor's glory,
and it will hold over the Ecce Homo.
Rest inside the repeated sentence for the decade.
It has not changed; it will not.

scripture.text: And the disciples hearing fell upon their face, and were very much afraid. And Jesus came and touched them: and said to them: Arise, and fear not.

meditations.body:
Glory floors them.
Human frailty cannot endure to look upon so great glory;
trembling through soul and body they fall — and cannot get up.
Note the quiet detail:
the saints in Scripture fall upon their faces; the wicked fall backwards.
Even collapse has a direction.
Then comes what may be the mystery's most human moment.
He approaches them, touches them gently,
that by His touch their fear might be banished
and their unnerved limbs regain strength;
He first banishes their fear, that He may afterward impart teaching.
The order is heaven's fixed etiquette:
no instruction until the fear is gone, and the fear goes by hand.
Arise, and fear not.
Whatever has flattened you lately, expect the touch before the lesson.

scripture.text: And they lifting up their eyes, saw no one, but only Jesus.

meditations.body:
Cloud gone, prophets gone, glory sheathed.
What remains, and it is everything: only Jesus.

scripture.text: And when Moses came down from the Mount Sinai, he held the two tables of the testimony, and he knew not that his face was horned from the conversation of the Lord.

meditations.body:
The mountain had a precedent.
Moses came down from Sinai not knowing that his face was horned
from the conversation of the Lord —
the Douay keeps Jerome's strange Latin, cornuta,
rays braided into horns of light,
the verse that put horns on Michelangelo's Moses.
But mark the difference.
Moses' face catches light like a moon:
borrowed from the conversation, fading afterward, soon needing a veil.
On Thabor the light is not caught but disclosed —
He is not shining from the conversation; He is the conversation.
Yet the precedent still preaches:
what a man beholds, he begins to resemble.
And Luke supplies the engine:
it was whilst He prayed that He was transfigured —
and it is in the soul that prays that He still does His transfiguring.
That is this Rosary's entire method, stated in two mountains.

scripture.text: And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying: Tell the vision to no man, till the Son of man be risen from the dead.

meditations.body:
Down the slope He imposes a gag order with an expiration date:
tell the vision to no man,
till the Son of Man be risen from the dead.
The pastoral logic is plain.
Published now, the marvel would seem incredible,
and the cross following after so great glory would cause offence.
Deeper still: had the people learned of this majesty,
love itself might have obstructed the Passion and so impeded redemption —
devotion as the last obstacle to salvation.
And the release date has a meaning:
keep silence until, filled with the Holy Ghost,
you can bear witness to spiritual deeds.
Some graces are issued sealed: provision, not publicity.
Even Thabor kept the Cross's schedule.
If God has shown you something, ask whether it came with a date.

scripture.text: For we have not by following artificial fables made known to you the power and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ: but we were eyewitnesses of his greatness. For he received from God the Father honour and glory, this voice coming down to him from the excellent glory: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Hear ye him. And this voice, we heard brought from heaven, when we were with him in the holy mount.

meditations.body:
Decades later, an old man writes to churches he will not see again
and reaches for his best evidence:
we were eyewitnesses of his greatness...
this voice we heard brought from heaven,
when we were with him in the holy mount.
This is the letter the Church reads on the Feast —
Peter, once ordered silent, finally spending Thabor,
and spending it as the Voice, not the light.
Notice his vocabulary a few lines earlier:
he calls his own dying body this tabernacle, soon to be laid away.
The man who offered to build three tabernacles learned he was one —
temporary, foldable, and full of glory anyway.
So the decade's question:
your mountain moments were issued as capital, not souvenirs.
Which one have you never once drawn on in a valley —
and who could you spend it on this week?

scripture.text: And he was transfigured before them. And his face did shine as the sun: and his garments became white as snow.

meditations.body:
Two words everyone skips: transfigured before them.
The Word of God has various forms,
appearing to each according as it is expedient for him,
and shows Himself to none beyond his capacity —
those who do not climb know only the carpenter's son;
those who ascend no longer know Him according to the flesh.
Then the garments.
His raiment is the words and sayings of the Gospels
with which Jesus is clothed —
or the saints themselves, white as snow with virtues.
Take the first reading literally tonight:
the Gospel page is His clothing.
Every time you read it slowly,
you are the woman in the crowd reaching for the hem —
and the hem, on Thabor's testimony, is made of light.

scripture.text: Dearly beloved, we are now the sons of God: and it hath not yet appeared what we shall be. We know that when he shall appear we shall be like to him: because we shall see him as he is.

meditations.body:
At the Jordan this arc opened with the verse before this one:
behold what manner of charity,
that we should be called the sons of God.
The next sentence looks up the family's future:
it hath not yet appeared what we shall be —
but when he shall appear, we shall be like to him,
because we shall see him as he is.
Thabor, then, is not only His preview;
it is the family photograph from ahead.
In this mystery Providence laid a solid foundation for the Church's hope:
that the whole body might know what transformation will be granted to it,
the members assured of sharing the glory that shone forth in their Head.
So the question, and answer it slowly:
do you actually believe that face is your future?
And if you did —
what are you gripping this week that you could afford to put down?

scripture.text: The north and the sea thou hast created. Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name:

meditations.body:
The mountain was on the psalter's map centuries early:
Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name —
a Galilean hill listed among creation's glad witnesses,
waiting all that time for its reason.
One afternoon the reason climbed it.
Now the descent.
Luke says the mountaintop conversation was of His decease,
which He should accomplish at Jerusalem —
so the road down from Thabor bends toward an upper room,
and the next decade is the last night.
Come down with Him the way the three did:
forbidden to chatter, carrying a Voice, walking toward a supper.
The luminous mysteries have one more light to show,
and it will be lamplight on bread.
Rejoice in His name on the way down.
The mountain, says the psalm, already does.

scripture.text: And whilst they were at supper, Jesus took bread and blessed and broke and gave to his disciples and said: Take ye and eat. This is my body.

meditations.body:
Set the clock before anything else:
this is the night before He dies,
and He knows the schedule better than the men arranging it.
In a few hours His body will be taken — seized, bound, handled by soldiers.
So watch what He does with the last free evening of that body:
whilst they were at supper, He took bread, and blessed, and broke,
and said take ye and eat: this is my body.
Given, before it can be grabbed.
The arrest will only ever collect what the supper has already surrendered;
Judas hands over a man who has just handed Himself over first —
to His friends, as food.
Every Mass since is that same maneuver, still standing.
Take your seat at the table for this decade.
The seating was never capped at twelve.

scripture.text: Before the festival day of the pasch, Jesus knowing that his hour was come, that he should pass out of this world to the Father: having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them unto the end.

meditations.body:
In finem dilexit: unto the end.
And the first shape the end took was supper.

scripture.text: And whilst they were at supper, Jesus took bread and blessed and broke and gave to his disciples and said: Take ye and eat. This is my body.

meditations.body:
Barely can the paradoxes stay in single file.
The Lord invites His servants to set before them Himself for food —
but who would dare to eat his Lord?
This food, when eaten, refreshes and does not fail:
He lives after being eaten, who rose after being put to death.
Nor is He diminished by distribution:
divided into parts in the Sacrament, He remains whole —
He is all in heaven, He is all in thy heart.
One line compresses the whole supper:
the Lord Jesus was at once guest and feast,
the eater and the things eaten.
Host, in both senses of the word.
Hold the great clause through the decade: whole in heaven, whole in you.
The arithmetic of love does not divide.

scripture.text: If any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world.

meditations.body:
Refuse every softening.
The bread taken by us in the mysteries
is not only the sign of Christ's flesh but is itself the very flesh —
for He does not say the bread I will give is the sign of my flesh,
but is my flesh.
Then answer the obvious shudder with unexpected tenderness:
why do we not see the flesh?
Because if it were seen, it would revolt us and we could not partake;
in condescension to our infirmity,
the mystical food is given under an appearance suited to our minds.
The veil is not evasion but mercy.
And the image for the union has never been bettered:
heated iron remains iron, with the fire's action in it —
so this flesh quickens, being the flesh of the Word.

scripture.text: And taking the chalice, he gave thanks and gave to them, saying: Drink ye all of this. For this is my blood of the new testament, which shall be shed for many unto remission of sins.

meditations.body:
With the chalice, notice the manners of the host:
drink ye all of it — and He first drank His own blood,
to lead them without fear into the communion of these mysteries.
No one is asked to go first but Him.
Then the ancient ledger:
the Old Testament had the blood of sheep and goats;
the New has the Lord's own.
The lamb's blood in Egypt bought the firstborn's lives for one night;
this Blood is shed unto remission of sins.
And weigh the famous word:
not for a few, nor for all, but for many —
because He came to redeem not a single nation
but many out of all nations.
Count the nations represented in your parish some Sunday morning.
The chalice predicted every one of them.

scripture.text: He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord: He hath given food to them that fear him. He will be mindful for ever of his covenant:

meditations.body:
Two words carry the mystery: in mei memoriam.
Besides renewing His immolation,
Christ desired to make of the Eucharist, in addition, a memorial —
the altar is another Calvary,
where the Cross is commemorated, represented and reproduced;
the testament of His love.
And the psalter sang the mystery in prophecy a thousand years early:
he hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works...
he hath given food to them that fear him.
Memorial and meal, fused in one verse.
Now the memorial's reach:
in Communion, Christ gives Himself
in the substantial totality of His works and mysteries.
Every decade you have prayed tonight —
river, wedding, kingdom, mountain — is contained in the Host.
The Rosary in your hand is, on the altar, a single small white circle.

scripture.text: Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new paste, as you are unleavened. For Christ our pasch is sacrificed. Therefore, let us feast, not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness: but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

meditations.body:
The old law never let a sacrifice end at the altar.
The Passover lamb was not only slain;
it had to be eaten, that night, by the household —
a sacrifice completed by a supper, or not completed at all.
Now hear Paul: Christ our pasch is sacrificed — therefore let us feast.
The therefore is the whole theology.
At the Jordan, the first public title of His ministry
was the name of a sacrifice: behold the Lamb of God.
At this table the title comes due in full,
because a lamb, in Israel, is not only offered but served.
Communion, then, is not a devotion appended to the sacrifice;
it is the sacrifice arriving at its table.
The Lamb was always meant to be supper.
Leaving the plate untouched leaves the Pasch unfinished.

scripture.text: He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood abideth in me: and I in him.

meditations.body:
Rank the mysteries by what they give the eye.
At Bethlehem a star helped; at the Jordan the heavens opened;
on Thabor the Divinity shone through the veil.
On the Cross the Godhead alone lay hid —
but here the Manhood hides as well.
The Eucharist is the mysterium fidei in its purest state,
resting solely on the words this is my body.
And exactly there is the consolation:
Christ, ever living, acts in silence, but sovereignly,
in the innermost depths of the soul, to transform it into Himself —
and if fervent souls feel only dryness after receiving,
let them be reassured and remain in peace.
He that eateth my flesh abideth in me, and I in him.
Abide is not visit.
Rest there for this decade: felt or unfelt, you are where He lives.

scripture.text: Many therefore of his disciples, hearing it, said: This saying is hard; and who can hear it?

meditations.body:
His Eucharistic catechesis was the least popular sermon He ever preached.
This saying is hard, who can hear it —
they answered for themselves: they could not.
Yet the fault lay in their fatuity, not in the difficulty of the truths.
Hold the principle every teacher since has clung to:
God's mysteries should draw men's attention, not enmity.
And take the scene's strange consolation:
He spoke the truth, and many were destroyed by it —
and He is not disturbed,
for He knew from the beginning who would believe.
He watched a congregation walk out rather than soften one sentence.
Whatever else the Real Presence is,
it is not a doctrine anyone invented to fill pews.

scripture.text: And Simon Peter answered him: Lord, to whom shall we go? Thou hast the words of eternal life. And we have believed and have known that thou art the Christ, the Son of God.

meditations.body:
Then said Jesus to the twelve: will you also go away?
The question was the right way to retain them.
He does not say go, which would cast them off,
but asks — freeing their staying from all shame and necessity,
for to stay from necessity would be the same as going away.
Love will not keep anyone by the sleeve.
Peter answers for the house in a speech of the greatest love:
Lord, to whom shall we go?
As if he said: Thou castest us from Thee —
then give us another to whom we shall go, if we leave Thee...
in Thy flesh and blood Thou givest what Thou art Thyself.
There is no other counter where the words of eternal life are sold.
When the teaching is hard,
the question is never really whether, but where else.

scripture.text: But Melchisedech, the king of Salem, bringing forth bread and wine, for he was the priest of the most high God,

meditations.body:
The oldest priest in Scripture appears from nowhere,
blesses Abram, and offers — of all things — bread and wine.
Hear the rhyme across two thousand years:
the typical Passover concluded,
the Lord comes to the true paschal sacrament,
that as Melchisedech, priest of the most high God,
had done in foreshadowing Him, offering bread and wine,
He also should offer the present verity of His Body and Blood.
Press the astonishing corollary:
the Christian mysteries are older than the Jewish —
Melchisedech's table predates Sinai.
And over it all stands the psalm's oath:
thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech,
an order whose one recorded liturgy is bread and wine.
Tonight the order's founder is outranked by its Fulfiller.

scripture.text: But let a man prove himself: and so let him eat of that bread and drink of the chalice. For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily eateth and drinketh judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord.

meditations.body:
The severest mercy in this mystery is one sentence:
Peter and Judas received of the same bread —
but Peter to life, Judas to death.
Same table, same hands, same gift;
the difference was entirely in the guest.
Which is why Paul legislates a checkpoint:
let a man prove himself, and so eat —
for the undiscerning eater eats judgment.
Not a velvet rope to keep you out; a mirror by the door.
So the decade's question is the practical one: how do you arrive?
Next Mass, arrive as Peter —
examined, honest about the one thing you already know needs confessing,
and hungry anyway.
If it has been a while since you stood at the mirror,
name the day this week you will.
Then come to the table free.

scripture.text: For we, being many, are one bread, one body: all that partake of one bread.

meditations.body:
What the elements are made of preaches.
Bread is made of many grains, wine is pressed from many berries —
and in choosing them, the Lord hallowed at His own table
the mystery of our peace and unity.
The Sacrament of the Body builds the Body:
we being many are one bread, one body.
Then the acclamation that has rung for sixteen centuries:
O sacrament of mercy, O sign of unity, O bond of love!
Whoso wishes to live, let him draw nigh, believe, be incorporated,
that he may be quickened.
You do not merely receive the Body of Christ;
you consent to be milled into it —
and the difficult person three pews over is your co-grain.
Communion has never once been private.

scripture.text: And I say to you, I will not drink from henceforth of this fruit of the vine until that day when I shall drink it with you new in the kingdom of my Father.

meditations.body:
He ends the first Mass with a toast postponed:
I will not drink of this fruit of the vine
until that day when I shall drink it with you new
in the kingdom of my Father.
A vow with a reunion date —
He rises having appointed a cup, and a company: with you.
The vow is already partly honored at the resurrection meals:
we ate and drank with him after he rose.
And the Canticle's wine cellar adds the room itself to the rhyme:
the Church entered that cellar most of all at Pentecost —
in the very cenacle where Christ kept His last supper —
so filled that mockers said, these men are full of new wine.
The vintage has begun.
At Cana the steward learned His cellar keeps the good wine until now.
So, plainly: if the Bridegroom is saving a cup for you,
what are you doing about Sunday?

scripture.text: And he said to me: Write: Blessed are they that are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he saith to me: These words of God are true.

meditations.body:
Cana's promise comes home to close the luminous mysteries:
a ministry that opened with wine at a wedding
ends history at a wedding —
blessed are they that are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb.
The whole Song of Songs was read as this wedding's libretto,
and its table-line — eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated —
is the Bridegroom's own invitation,
honored above all in the sacred mysteries of the Eucharist.
Between the first course and the last stands this supper,
repeated on every altar until he come.
Then mark how the night continues:
a hymn being said, they went out unto mount Olivet.
The seam between the Rosary's light and its sorrow
is a few hundred meters of hymn, the Cedron below.
End the decade at table, called and blessed;
and when you rise, rise as they did: singing, and going with Him.
